scope: 32 feature-gap targets; source states and evidence are deliberately separate. Historical common-profile passes are contextual, never automatic target qualification.

adapter-file.boundary: Linux C adapter over Legacy native file storage. Each feature has separate reference/artifact evidence; historical common-v1 logical behavior uses compatibility scans/buffers and native formats.

file-legacy.boundary: Public default; native duplicates, savepoints, borrowed snapshots, backup and manual maintenance exist. New backlog targets require their own evidence.

file-cohort.boundary: Shared native API, different publication metadata; Legacy evidence does not independently qualify its publication/lifecycle behavior.

file-indexed.boundary: Shared native API, indexed publication metadata; retain separate migration/publication/lifecycle gates.

resident.boundary: Experimental bounded anonymous pool implements authenticated checkpoints, automatic WAL rotation/growth, Tiny reuse, nested savepoints, explicit65536-database catalogs, persisted integer/reverse/custom key and duplicate ordering, KV/IP values up to16MiB, variable/fixed duplicate values up to65536 bytes, and checksum/encryption for WAL/checkpoints. Captured snapshots export atomically to complete independently reopenable Resident environments through Linux/macOS/Windows source backends while later source writes continue; Coordinated independent read-only capture is implemented on Linux/macOS/Windows after explicit identity-bound protocol negotiation (Unix flag1, full 128-bit Windows flag2); readers replay into owned pages under byte/graph limits and return Busy on contention. Replication remains in development. Keys cap4080 bytes, per-tail WAL256MiB; explicit pool/undo/decode/metadata budgets apply.

hybrid.boundary: Experimental backend with existing checkpoint and retirement APIs; evaluate reuse without inheriting qualification.

range-v6.boundary: Experimental format6; range-lifecycle implements independent read-only capture/export, typed named retention, physical reader leases, explicit graph compaction, pack rotation and leased whole-pack reclamation. Replication remains unsupported; adapter access remains unqualified or unsupported. The backend remains experimental and is not promoted.

implementation_summary: All twelve extension APIs have production implementations. Native comparator indexes, direct reserve buffers, actual allocation/tree statistics and explicit large-value profiles are implemented. The 64-bit maximum is 4,294,967,295 bytes per value; smaller profiles retain their original envelopes. Focused source tests are listed in implementation_tests; canonical target states, counts and receipts below are unchanged.

Ordinary coordinated Native/C file owners now enable automatic bounded maintenance on Linux, macOS and Windows, with explicit finite history retention and protected reader/named bases. Linux reusable fixed layouts retain v2 bytes. macOS/Windows reusable slots use the M3 full 128-bit wire and a dedicated lease file; genuine platform reservations, writable slots, authenticated read-only checksum backing and lifetime quota ownership are implemented. Windows accepts and ignores NORDAHEAD, as the pinned reference does.

Resident coordinated read-only capture now has all three source platforms: Unix flag1 bytes remain unchanged and Windows flag2 hashes the complete file identity. Cold file payload-header scalar reads use short independent scopes, preserving extent validation without retaining large value windows. Native file CLI reads/checks/copies use a real coordinated snapshot pin beside an active writer; Range keeps its existing route.

Native/C chunked reads, writes, copies and replay, persisted Resident ordering, explicit 65,536-database catalogs, Range6 compaction/rotation/leased reclamation and private-spool operator large fields remain implemented. Common M3 codec/lease and three-format CLI witnesses pass on Linux. Windows GNU DLL/Native binaries and the complete operator/importer/launcher/two-exporter package link; the macOS Rust C static library release build passes. Darwin tool source is integrated, but SDK C utility builds and Windows/macOS runtime parity are not claimed. Resource/performance and broader platform qualification remain open.

External C database-name limits now follow the selected key profile, including the modern stored NUL. Modern empty named databases remain distinct from MAIN; legacy empty names remain rejected. Native dump v2 distinguishes MAIN/named explicitly while retaining v1 input, and migration preserves named empty sections. Focused codec tests do not change qualification states or counts.

Resident atomic snapshot export now has Linux/macOS/Windows source backends; builds and Linux checks do not establish other-host runtime parity. The existing four-mode Linux 256 KiB WAL/64-slot witness preserves old borrows and cold restarts through more than ten WAL capacities while accounting linked and deleted-open assets, allocated bytes, RSS and OS high-water growth. Current Root observes 438,272 allocated bytes maximum at sampled boundaries and 1,720,320 bytes RSS/high-water growth within predeclared limits; after reader release allocated bytes are 274,432 and owner close retains zero asset FDs. Thirty-six checkpoint fail/death cuts and eighteen real I/O cases also pass. These focused results do not close M5 or change canonical states/counts.

C MAP_RESIZED admission now follows actual selected logical growth at begin/renew/writer entry, including Native-only commits; a larger size hint alone does not reject a fitting view. mapsize=0 adopts capacity with an actual minimum clamp, preserving old borrows/reset/reader slots. Exact UUID/checkpoint scalar certificates avoid repeated walks of known views; unfamiliar checkpoints can still walk metadata once, and resource/I/O failures never become size certificates. Focused same-executable pinned-reference and Native-peer tests do not establish O(1), platform or full performance acceptance.
